subject: Finex Health: overlap of CDN maintenance & partial-path failover — request for apportionment
messages:
From: Avery Liao <avery.liao@finex.health>
To: ops@redwood.com; sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected partial failures during 2027-09-14 CDN maintenance window

Hi team,

We pulled logs for the 09/14 22:45–23:15 UTC window and are seeing a ~12 minute stretch where ~7% of traffic to our /api/generate endpoints returned 504s or experienced tokenization timeouts. Our pager identified it as a partial degradation (only requests routed via the us-east-1 edge returned higher latency).

Edgewave (our CDN) sent a maintenance notice for 09/14 22:00–23:00 UTC (attached). They claim a planned handoff between two POPs that affected some BGP advertisements. We understand scheduled maintenance may reduce credit eligibility, but the scope and routing overlap means some of our users hit degraded responses while others did not.

We need:
- Your official uptime accounting for that window and whether it is treated as maintenance-excluded.
- The apportionment logic used if a third party (Edgewave) initiated an overlap that caused a partial path failure.
- Any available telemetry (probe traces, per-pop error rates) to support an uptime credit request with our procurement team.

Attached: subset of Finex telemetry for the affected time and Edgewave notice.

Thanks,
Avery Liao
SRE, Finex Health
ops+uptime@finex.health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Avery Liao <avery.liao@finex.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@edgewave-cdn.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected partial failures during 2027-09-14 CDN maintenance window

Hi Avery — thanks for the heads up and for attaching the telemetry. We'll look into this immediately. Quick points up front:

- We see correlated token timeout spikes in our telemetry for requests that traversed the us-east-1 edge between 22:43–22:55 UTC.
- Redwood's SLA excludes customer-notified maintenance windows only if the maintenance was initiated on our side or on a third party that Redwood explicitly lists in the published third-party exclusion matrix. Edgewave is a 3rd-party transit/CDN provider; we do not automatically classify all external vendor maintenance as an exclusion.

Immediate ask to you and Edgewave: can Edgewave provide their POP-level BGP rota changes and any propagation timestamps? That will help determine whether the event originated inside their network and whether the impact matches their maintenance window.

Marissa/Ben — I'll need a quick apportionment proposal from the SLA team: how to attribute the 12-minute partial degradation across (a) Redwood serving runtime, (b) Edgewave handoff, and (c) customer routing. Ben, can you pull the routing/probe crosswalk and a token-level request sample from our ingress?

I'll follow up with a proposed timeline for a formal credit determination.

—Sean
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@edgewave-cdn.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Avery Liao <avery.liao@finex.health>
Date: 2027-09-16T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Edgewave maintenance window and routing handoff

Hi all,

Edgewave performed the planned POP handoff in us-east-1 on 2027-09-14 at 22:04 UTC; BGP updates were propagated by 22:18 UTC. We observed transient re-advertisements affecting ~3% of our AS paths between 22:16–22:28 UTC. Our internal monitors did not show increased origin loss beyond 22:28, but we did see reroutes that increased RTT for specific prefixes until upstream caches refreshed (~22:40 UTC).

I'll attach the per-POP BGP events export and a short reconciliation file. From our perspective, the primary disruption window is 22:16–22:28 UTC (transient re-advertisements) with elevated RTT until ~22:40 UTC.

—Oliver
Edgewave — Network Ops
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Liao <avery.liao@finex.health>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-17T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood apportionment proposal for 2027-09-14 partial degradation

Avery — thanks to you and Oliver for the artifacts. Ben and I reviewed the combined telemetry (Finex subset + Edgewave BGP events + Redwood ingress traces). Below is our proposed reasoning and calculation for credit eligibility:

Summary of findings:
- Impact window observed in user-facing errors: 22:43–22:55 UTC (12 minutes).
- Edgewave reports transient BGP re-adverts earlier (22:16–22:28) and RTT elevation until ~22:40. There is a mismatch between Edgewave's internal timeline and the user-observed error window — the alignment suggests an interplay of cache evictions and our routing convergence.
- Error traffic was localized to the us-east-1 POP and represented ~7% of Finex's total requests in the window.

Apportionment rationale (proposed):
- Treat the initial Edgewave re-advert events (22:16–22:28) as a third-party maintenance event. This portion is excluded from Redwood's uptime tally, provided evidence is produced (Edgewave export attached).
- The user-facing error window (22:43–22:55) falls after Edgewave reports restored origin reachability; given the temporal gap, we consider that Redwood's routing convergence + prefix cache behavior amplified the residual impact. Therefore we propose splitting the 12-minute impact as follows: 60% attributable to Edgewave (initial instability + cache churn), 40% attributable to Redwood ingress routing and our prefix-refresh handling.

Credit calculation example (proposed):
- Finex observed 12 minutes of partial degradation, weighted by affected traffic share (~7% of total). For a monthly uptime percentage calculation we would apply a proportional credit for the weighted time attributed to Redwood (40% of 12 minutes = 4.8 minutes).

Next steps & deliverables:
1) Ben to produce a per-minute request/error histogram and the precise token counts for the affected 12 minutes (ETA: EOD 2027-09-17).
2) Edgewave to provide signed BGP event export and a short note confirming the maintenance start/stop timestamps (requested).
3) Sean to coordinate a formal SLA determination and, if approved, a credit issuance or billing adjustment.

Attachments referenced: finex_telemetry_subset_0913-0915.zip, edgewave-maintenance-notice-20270914.pdf

If Finex wants us to waive Redwood's apportioned portion pending goodwill, we can escalate to finance for a discretionary credit, but our default is to apply the split above.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, SLA Decisions
Redwood Inference

From: Avery Liao <avery.liao@finex.health>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@edgewave-cdn.com>
Date: 2027-09-18T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood apportionment proposal for 2027-09-14 partial degradation

Marissa/Sean — appreciate the thorough analysis and the proposed split. A few quick items from Finex:

- We accept the request for Edgewave signed BGP export and will treat that as supporting evidence.
- Our procurement will need the explicit minute-level weighted calculation to file a credit request; please include the exact token counts and the final minutes attributed to Redwood.
- Given the business impact (telemetry indicates several failed patient-facing requests), Finex requests expedited review and credit issuance within the current billing cycle if Redwood's apportioned minutes remain > 0.

Can Ben share the per-minute histogram and token counts in the next 24 hours? Also looping in our procurement contact (procure+finex@finex.health) in case we need a DocuSign amendment.

Thanks — looking forward to closure.

—Avery
SRE, Finex Health
